Privacy Policy

Ponlet Privacy Policy

Last Updated: October 3, 2026
Platforms: Android (jp.yasagure.ponlet), Web, iOS, Desktop

Transferred Content and Diagnostics

Connections are established directly via peer-to-peer (WireGuard / WebRTC DataChannel) whenever possible. In environments where NAT traversal or firewall restrictions make direct connection difficult, packets are relayed through DERP relay servers. Transfer packets passing through DERP remain end-to-end encrypted (E2EE) with WireGuard, so those relays do not hold the decryption keys. Ponlet does not operate a file storage server retaining transferred content. Analytics, diagnostics, and OS backups are handled separately.

01

Overview & Data Handling

Core Principles

This Privacy Policy outlines how Ponlet ("the App") handles data. The App encompasses the Android client (package name: jp.yasagure.ponlet), the Web client, iOS client, and desktop versions (macOS/Windows/Linux).

The App transfers files and text to a peer chosen by the user using encryption. We do not operate a centralized storage server to retain or view transferred content. Analytics and diagnostics for quality improvements are separately sent to Google.

No Account Required
Accounts & Identity

Normal use does not require an account or login or ask for your name, email address, or phone number. SDK installation identifiers are described in Section 4.

No Transfer Storage Server
Files & Messages

Ponlet does not operate a transfer storage server retaining photos, documents, or text. Local storage, export to other apps, and OS backup or migration copies are handled separately.

Opt-Out Telemetry
Telemetry (Usage Reporting)

Limited telemetry for quality improvement is provided on an opt-out basis (enabled by default; it can be turned off in Settings). No advertising SDKs are included, and transferred content such as file names or message text is not passed to Ponlet’s custom analytics events. See "4. Telemetry" for details.

02

Communication Architecture & DERP Relays

P2P & Encrypted Relay

Communications are established directly between devices via peer-to-peer (WireGuard / WebRTC DataChannel) whenever possible. In restrictive environments—such as symmetric NAT or strict corporate firewalls—packets are relayed through public DERP (Designated Encrypted Relay for Packets) relay servers.

  • End-to-End Encryption (E2EE): Transfer packets relayed through DERP are encrypted between devices using WireGuard, and the relays do not hold the decryption keys. Analytics and diagnostic transmissions are separate communications.
  • Connection Information: Establishing a peer connection involves network addresses and routing information. These connection details are separate from the encrypted file and message contents.
  • Confidential Invite Links: The 32-byte shared cryptographic key is embedded exclusively in the URL hash fragment (#i=...). Under the HTTP standard, hash fragments are handled entirely by the browser client and are never sent across the network to hosting servers (such as Cloudflare Pages) or logged in server logs.
03

Local Data Storage

Device-Level Management

Received files and text are managed on your device. Copies exported by the user or created through OS backup or migration are handled separately:

Web Client
Volatile Browser Memory

Transferred files are temporarily held in browser memory (Blob) and written to your Downloads folder only when you choose to save them. Closing the browser tab immediately purges the memory.

Native Apps
Local Storage Directory

Android stores received files in Ponlet’s internal app storage rather than automatically saving them to public Downloads. Choosing “Open” grants the selected compatible app read access to that file. iOS and desktop apps use their respective app storage or download folders.

This Android revision is configured to exclude received files from OS cloud backup on Android 12 (API31) and higher. It preserves the existing scope of device-to-device migration (D2D). Backup of app settings and D2D copies or restoration depend on device settings, OS, and manufacturer behavior. This change does not delete backup copies created by older versions.

On Android, the camera is used to scan an invitation QR code when the user chooses the camera scanner; permission is requested at that point. ML Kit processes camera images and scan results on the device and does not use them for transmission to Google. The app reads files selected by the user through Android’s document picker. Text copy, paste, and sharing also follow user actions.

04

Telemetry (Usage Reporting)

Opt-Out Telemetry

The App includes opt-out telemetry (usage reporting) for the purpose of quality improvement and stability. Telemetry is enabled by default and can be turned off at any time from Settings (the gear icon at the top of the app).

  • Google Analytics for Firebase (Analytics): Used on iOS / Android / Web.
  • Firebase Crashlytics: Used on iOS / Android. Sends crash reports when a crash occurs (including native crash stack traces).
  • Android ML Kit (QR scanning): The SDK may send diagnostics such as device, OS and app information, installation-related identifiers, performance, and API usage to Google. These diagnostics are separate from on-device image and scan-result processing and are not stopped by the Firebase telemetry switch.
  • Google Analytics 4 Measurement Protocol (direct HTTP POST): Used on Desktop only. Enabled only when configured via environment variables.

Custom Android events: app_start, session_created, peer_connected, transfer_started, transfer_completed, transfer_cancelled, text_message_sent / text_message_received, error

Custom Android parameters: Platform, OS and app versions, language, file count, transport, direction, message-length bracket, cancellation reason, and error category. SDK automatic collection is separate from this list.

Custom Event Exclusions
What Telemetry Does Not Include

Ponlet’s custom events do not include file names, contents, message bodies, peer addresses, session keys, or invitation URLs. On Android, Firebase Analytics handles app-instance identifiers, app usage events, and coarse location derived from IP addresses. SDK identifiers can exist without a login.

Crash Reports
What Crashlytics May Include

Reports may include stack traces, device and app state, OS and app versions, and installation-related identifiers. On Android, dependent SDK identifiers and session information also need to be considered.

How to Opt Out
Turning Telemetry Off

Turning off "Allow telemetry" in Settings disables the collection settings for Firebase Analytics and Crashlytics. Android stores this choice in app preferences; Web uses browser storage and Desktop uses app settings. On Android, Crashlytics applies OFF on the next app launch and keeps crash information locally while disabled. Turning it on again sends previously unsent reports. Android QR SDK diagnostics are separate from this switch. Turning it off does not delete previously stored analytics or diagnostics or disable all OS backup.

When telemetry is enabled, the data described above is sent to Google LLC (Firebase / Google Analytics). See the Google Privacy Policy for details.

Along with enabling telemetry, this policy may be updated together with the services involved (Firebase, etc.). Any significant changes will be announced on this page.

05

Third-Party Services

Services & Advertising Purposes

This Android revision disables Firebase Analytics Advertising ID collection and ad personalization and removes the Advertising ID, AdServices Advertising ID, and advertising attribution permissions. This does not remove app-instance identifiers, IP-derived coarse location, or Crashlytics and ML Kit diagnostics. Existing internal-test version 1.0.18 (versionCode 2026093037) included advertising identifier permissions; this description does not apply to that older version. This revision candidate has the same versionName and versionCode 2030000102.

The App does not display ads and is not intended to use usage data for advertising, marketing, or sale to data brokers. Firebase and Android’s ML Kit are Google LLC services. Telemetry collection settings, QR SDK diagnostics, and peer transfers are separate paths.

We do not operate a server retaining transferred files or messages. This does not guarantee that Google or other services retain no analytics or diagnostic data.

06

Google Play & Children's Privacy

Disclosures & Audience

This page describes data handling in the apps, including Android. Google Play disclosures must be checked against the distributed version and actual service settings.

  • Children's Privacy: The Android app is intended for general users and is not designed as a child-directed app. This does not mean that SDK identifiers or diagnostics are not collected.
  • Data Deletion & Access Requests: Normal use does not create an account. Clearing app data or uninstalling removes current local Android app data. It does not guarantee deletion of copies in other apps, external storage, migrated devices, existing OS backups, or Google analytics and diagnostics. For questions about retention and deletion, contact app-support@mat2uken.app.
